newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPALS - Munis close down 1/4 point.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPALS - Munis close down 1/4 point.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices limped to a lower close Monday as players eyed both the week's tax-exempt calendar and U.S. government market auction.
"I have (muni prices) down a little on the day--a couple of basis points, maybe 1/8 to 1/4--but very light trading, extremely light," a muni trader said.

A municipal analyst described the broader market as down about 1/4 point, with high-grades down two basis points overall in light trade. Dollar bonds opened down 1/8 to 1/4 point, were down 1/4 point at noon EDT and stayed there for the session's remainder, he said.

While a few bid lists circulated, a trader said he expected more given Friday's bond market selloff. Bonds slipped after July non-farm payrolls came in stronger than expected, and the July National Association of Purchasing Management Index suggested strength.

In the government market Monday, the benchmark 30-year bond was down 14/32 at 101-27/32 to yield 6.48 percent shortly before 1700 EDT Monday. The U.S. Treasury is scheduled to sell $16 billion in three-year notes on Tuesday, $12 billion in 10-year notes on Wednesday, and $10 billion in 30-year bonds on Thursday.
In debt futures, the September municipal contract closed down 2/32 at 120-14/32. The September T-bond contract closed down 5/32 at 114-21/32. The MOB spread is 185 ticks.
Meanwhile, new municipal offerings are expected to hit $3.9 billion this week.
"There's a decent calendar," a trader said. "It's going to be a good test to see if the buyers are out there and (if they) take advantage of the fact that we are down 20 basis points in one day."
Tuesday's sales are expected to total $2 billion in 43 offerings, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Negotiated offerings totalled $1.2 billion in 19 sales, with a $300 million New York City Municipal Water Finance Authority offering through PaineWebber Inc topping the list.
"I'm watching Waters, but I think Georgia GOs would be interesting the way it's structured," the trader said, adding that the Georgia deal features non-callable bonds.
Georgia's $240 million offering at 1100 EDT Tuesday is the largest of the 24 competitive sales totaling $735 million that are scheduled Tuesday.
